title: One defect, one score
statement: Map each kind of defect to a single criterion and score in one place, so a fault can't fail several criteria or land on different scores across runs.
detail: A base rule and a free-response overlay mapped the same answer-key defects to different scores, and because both layers applied to the same items, one defect could be tagged to different scores across runs, the instability the change targeted. The base layer now defers score assignment to the type layer instead of asserting a competing one. The lesson rubric states that each issue maps to exactly one primary score, and a per-option lint was kept report-only so that it adds detail without double-counting the score. Mapped this way, a fault is also never counted twice.
against: The local judge's prompt lets one issue zero several criteria: '2. Every issue MUST result in at least one 0.0 dimension' (`icloud-work/evaluator/ap_benchmark/prompts/base.py`, line 65).
